title: Dynamics 365 ERP apps plugin for Copilot Cowork: work with finance and operations data in Cowork
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, prerequisites, licensing and admin controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. The plugin-blocking guidance should clarify that blocking applies to new conversations; conversations already using the plugin continue until they end.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The Dynamics 365 ERP apps plugin lets Cowork users read finance and operations apps data in a conversation.
claims.quote: You can work with ERP data alongside email, documents, and other Microsoft 365 services in a single conversational experience.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The plugin can change finance and operations apps records.
claims.quote: Data tools – Read, create, update, and delete records in finance and operations apps data entities.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Cowork combines ERP capabilities with email, documents and spreadsheets in one conversational experience.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork combines these ERP capabilities with its built-in Work IQ features (email, calendar, documents, spreadsheets) to orchestrate workflows that span multiple systems.

claims.claim: The plugin connects Cowork to a finance and operations apps environment through the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server.
claims.quote: The Dynamics 365 ERP apps plugin connects Copilot Cowork to your finance and operations apps environment through the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server.

claims.claim: The MCP endpoint exposes ERP tools and operations to agents.
claims.quote: The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server provides a dynamic framework for agents to perform data operations and access the business logic of finance and operations apps.

claims.claim: Users can ask Cowork to orchestrate workflows spanning ERP systems, email and documents.
claims.quote: users can ask Copilot Cowork to retrieve ERP data, perform operations, and orchestrate business workflows that span ERP systems, email, documents, and other Microsoft 365 services.

claims.claim: The plugin uses the dynamic Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server.
claims.quote: The Dynamics 365 ERP apps plugin uses the dynamic Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server.

claims.where: What's changing: tool categories; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Data tools perform create, read, update and delete operations through data entities.
claims.quote: Data tools in the MCP server enable the agent to work with application data through data entities. The agent can use these tools to perform Create, Read, Update, Delete (CRUD) operations

claims.where: What's changing: tool categories; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Form tools perform operations available on application pages, including changes to application data.
claims.quote: Rather than having static tools for specific actions, like Find approved vendors or Release purchase requisition lines, the agent uses the tools to open forms, set field values, and select actions available on the form.

claims.claim: Action tools invoke secured business logic that developers expose.
claims.quote: Action tools – Invoke secured business logic that developers explicitly expose through the MCP server.

claims.claim: A user installs the Dynamics 365 ERP apps plugin from Discover in Cowork.
claims.quote:
Select the + button, select Customize, and then select Discover.
Locate the Dynamics 365 ERP apps plugin, and then select Install.

claims.quote: Find the Finance & Operations connector, and then select Configure.

claims.quote:

claims.where: What's changing: installation; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An administrator can deploy the plugin to selected users or groups from the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: An administrator can deploy the Dynamics 365 ERP apps plugin to selected users or groups from the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The plugin's Learn enable and use pages carry no preview label.
claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 ERP apps Cowork rollout release channel wave; read the complete enable-copilot-cowork-erp and use-copilot-cowork-erp pages, including prerequisites and limitations. Neither labels this plugin preview.

claims.where: What's changing: Learn versus roadmap; Open questions
claims.claim: The plugin's Learn enable and use pages state no selected-customer restriction.
claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 ERP apps Cowork rollout release channel wave; read enable-copilot-cowork-erp and use-copilot-cowork-erp in full. Their prerequisites and limitations state licensing, environment and regional restrictions, not selected-preview-customer eligibility.

claims.claim: Learn documents the plugin on Cowork web, Outlook, Teams, desktop and mobile surfaces.
claims.quote: you can use it in Copilot Cowork on the web, in Outlook and Teams, in the Microsoft Copilot desktop app for Windows and Mac, and in the Microsoft Copilot mobile app.

claims.claim: Plugin installation and connector setup use the Cowork web experience.
claims.quote: Use the Cowork web experience to install the plugin and configure its connector.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: MCP operations run under the authenticated user's identity.
claims.quote: Operations run under the authenticated user's identity and security context in finance and operations apps.

claims.claim: The MCP server does not elevate privilege.
claims.quote: The MCP server doesn't elevate privilege.

claims.claim: Existing ERP roles, duties and privileges limit the data and operations a Cowork user can access.
claims.quote: The roles, duties, privileges, record-level security, and data security policies assigned to that user apply to every request.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The plugin is admin-opt-in because users cannot use it until administrators configure the required access and billing.
claims.quote:
Before users can install and use the Dynamics 365 ERP apps plugin, ensure that:
Each user has an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
An administrator enabled Copilot Cowork in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Administrator enablement of Cowork is a plugin prerequisite.
claims.quote: An administrator enabled Copilot Cowork in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Usage-based billing and Copilot Credits must be configured for plugin users.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing and Copilot Credits are configured for the users who use the plugin.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[2].governs; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The plugin requires the tenant Dataverse integration setting to be enabled.
claims.quote: The Dynamics 365 ERP apps plugin requires that the Dataverse integration setting is enabled in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center.

claims.where: Why it matters: user acquisition; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Licensed users can acquire the plugin themselves when prerequisites and administrator availability policies permit it.
claims.quote: If an administrator or billing policy prevents installation, the plugin might show Request access instead of Install.

claims.claim: The MCP server does not store customer data.
claims.quote: It returns results to the calling client for the duration of the request, but doesn't store customer data.

claims.claim: Data movement or retention outside the ERP environment depends on the agent client's data handling policies.
claims.quote: Any data movement or retention outside the customer's finance and operations environment would be dependent on the data storage and retention policies of the agent client

claims.claim: The worldwide Cowork admin page points to Microsoft Purview for securing and governing Cowork.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview is available to secure and govern Cowork.

claims.claim: Cowork uses Anthropic models as a subprocessor for some capabilities.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork uses Anthropic models as a subprocessor for some capabilities.

claims.claim: The Anthropic capability is off by default in the EU, EFTA and UK.
claims.quote: This capability is off by default in the European Union (EU), European Free Trade Association (EFTA), and United Kingdom (UK)

claims.claim: Administrators in the EU, EFTA and UK must enable the Anthropic capability for their users to use it.
claims.quote: so administrators in those regions must enable it for their users.

claims.claim: The MCP server excludes system administration forms for security, user setup and Feature Management.
claims.quote: The MCP server doesn't provide access to some forms related to system admin tasks, like feature management, user management, and managing security.

claims.claim: The environment must be Tier 2 or above, or a Unified Developer Environment.
claims.quote: The environment must be Tier 2 or above, or a Unified Developer Environment.

claims.quote: Cloud Hosted Environments (CHE) and on-premises environments aren't supported.

Qualifying licenses include:

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Cowork usage is billed through consumption of Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork, Copilot Studio agents, and Work IQ API can consume Copilot credits from a shared tenant pool.

claims.claim: Cowork model responses count towards consumption.

claims.claim: Cowork tool calls, skill calls and other activities count towards consumption.
claims.quote: Activities such as model responses, tool and skill calls, image generation, and browser tasks count toward your organization's consumption.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: ERP MCP consumption
claims.claim: The Cowork ERP use page applies current MCP credit billing rules and premium exemptions to ERP MCP calls.
claims.quote: Calls to the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server can consume Copilot Credits according to the current MCP licensing rules, with applicable exemptions for qualifying premium licenses.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: ERP MCP rate
claims.claim: ERP MCP execution on clients other than Copilot Studio costs 0.1 Copilot Credits per tool call.
claims.quote: For agents built on other agent clients, usage of the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server incurs a cost of one copilot credit per 10 tool calls to the server (or 0.1 credits per tool call).

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: premium exemptions
claims.claim: Dynamics 365 Finance Premium and Supply Chain Management Premium users are exempt from ERP MCP execution billing on clients other than Copilot Studio.
claims.quote:
The following premium licenses are exempt from the tool execution billing for agents built on clients other than Copilot Studio.
Dynamics 365 Finance Premium
Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Premium

claims.claim: Cowork orchestration consumption is separate from ERP MCP execution billing.
claims.quote: This cost is an incremental charge by Microsoft for the execution of the MCP server. The cost for the LLM orchestration is a separate charge by the agent client for token consumption, based on the rates of that client.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: shared tenant pool
claims.claim: Cowork, Copilot Studio agents and Work IQ API can consume a shared tenant pool of credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork, Copilot Studio agents, and Work IQ API can consume Copilot credits from a shared tenant pool.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: spending limits; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Spending policies set spending limits for Cowork users.
claims.quote: Use spending policies in the Cost Management dashboard to control access and Copilot Credit spending for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Credit limits are spending safeguards, not real-time access gates, and enforcement is asynchronous.
claims.quote: Credit limits are a spending safeguard, not a real-time access gate. Credit consumption and limit enforcement are evaluated asynchronously

claims.where: Scope: Who gets it; controls[0].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users need to be in the scope of a spending policy selecting Cowork to have Cowork access.
claims.quote: A user has access to Cowork when a policy's scope includes them (directly through All users, or through a security group) and that policy selects Cowork under Select agents and services. If no policy in scope selects Cowork, the user has no access.

claims.claim: Plugin management requires a tenant administrator or the Copilot administrator role.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 admin center access: You must be a tenant administrator, or have the Copilot administrator role.

claims.claim: Accessing the tenant Copilot Dataverse settings requires the AI administrator or Global administrator role.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 admin role (AI administrator or Global administrator) to access Microsoft 365 admin center Copilot settings.

claims.claim: Learn states that Anthropic models are unavailable in government or sovereign clouds.
claims.quote: Anthropic models aren't available in government or sovereign clouds.

claims.claim: The plugin is available in regions where Copilot Cowork is deployed.
claims.quote: The plugin is currently available in regions where Copilot Cowork is deployed.

claims.claim: The pages read give no rollout wave or release channel for this plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 ERP apps Cowork rollout release channel wave. Read the plugin enable and use pages and the cited Cowork admin pages; no plugin rollout wave or release channel is specified. Search returned general Dynamics release schedules and Cowork June GA, not a plugin wave.

claims.claim: Cowork policy configuration is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Agents and services > Cowork.
claims.quote:
go to Copilot > Cost Management.
Select the Configuration tab.
Select the spending policy you want to edit.
The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes:
Scope
Agents and services

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/serviceSettings adds a service setting to an existing policy.
claims.quote:
APIs under the /beta version are subject to change.
Create spendingPolicyServiceSetting | POST /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/serviceSettings | Add a service to a policy.

claims.claim: The service-setting POST requires the parent policy's If-Match ETag.
claims.quote: If-Match | The ETag of the parent spending policy. Required.

claims.claim: The request body can set serviceId to cowork and state to enabled to govern Cowork through the policy.
claims.quote:
serviceId | String | The key identifying a governed service category, such as cowork or workIQ.
state | serviceSettingState | Whether the service is governed (enabled) or excluded (disabled). Required on create.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first row; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A low credit limit does not prevent Cowork access; policy scope controls the access grant.
claims.quote: A policy with a limit of one credit still grants access. To remove access for a user, remove them from every spending policy that includes Cowork. A low credit limit doesn't block access.

claims.claim: The plugin blocking control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > plugin > Users > Block.
claims.quote:
select Agents > Tools.
Find the plugin you want to manage and go to the Users tab.
Adjust the availability setting:
Select Block: No users in your tenant can access the plugin.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent usage.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Available to all users permits licensed Copilot users to find and acquire the plugin.
claims.quote: Available to all users: All licensed Copilot users in your tenant can find and acquire the plugin.

claims.claim: Available to specific users or groups scopes plugin visibility to those users or security groups.
claims.quote: Available to specific users or groups: Only the users or security groups you specify can view the plugin.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can block a plugin where they do not want users to access it.
claims.quote: Blocking takes effect for new conversations. Conversations already in progress that use the plugin continue until they end.
claims.fix: Append to controls[1].note and its rendered table note: 'Blocking takes effect for new conversations; conversations already using the plugin continue until they end.' This qualification is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/cowork/cowork-manage-plugins#block-a-plugin-thats-already-been-shared.

claims.claim: The Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.
